newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end easier, capped by G7.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end easier, capped by G7.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier in thin trade on Wednesday as interest dwindled ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) weekend summit and the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s tankan business sentiment survey next week.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 80 points easier at 20,570 after hitting an early low of 20,410 on low volume of 10,740 lots.

"We were in a 100-points range all afternoon. As the weekend comes closer, the trading range is going to get worse and worse because of the G7 and next week's tankan," said a trader at a Japanese futures house.
He said news of a 200 percent rise in Japan's May trade surplus triggered fears of trade tensions with the United States and a possible strengthening of the yen.
The dollar fell briefly against the yen earlier in the day as the trade surplus was near the top end of a forecast range but the decline was short-lived.
Comments by former Finance Ministry official Makoto Utsumi about Japan's current long-term interest rates being too low had little impact.
"He's not in a position to make any decisions anyway. I think the market is more affected by the G7 and the tankan now," the trader said.
He said the tankan was likely to reflect negative sentiment, partly due to the effects of a hike in Japan's consumption tax on April 1.
"The Nikkei should be in a 20,300-20,700 range if the dollar/yen doesn't move a lot and there's no major news," he said.
On Taiwan futures, the MSCI June contract ended at 372.0 against its opening 369.9 on volume of 1,060 lots.
